nate: Ran a deep profiling pass on the INT8 inference path — attaching nsys + perfetto traces. Seeing a recurring ~20-40ms CPU-side stall during KV cache warmup that lines up with host-side dequant work :confused:

nate: Command I ran:
```bash
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --sample=none -o run_int8_kv_warmup nvidia-docker run ...
perfetto --out trace.pbz --config perfetto_proto.cfg
```

nate: Quick observations from the flame view:
- GPU kernels look healthy overall (int8 GEMM kernels sub-1ms per launch)
- But there are repeated ~15-35ms gaps on the CPU timeline between kernel launches when KV hits occur
- These gaps correlate with `host_dequant_batch` tasks in our codepath (we offload dequant to CPU for now)

michelle: interesting — do the gaps coincide with small batch sizes? could be kernel launch overhead + CPU sync on memcpy.

nate: yes, most of the impacted requests are small (<32 tokens, single-example) and batching window is 3ms. I suspect we often send 1-2 example batches that trigger host dequant + H2D memcpy that blocks.

sam: can you paste the perf counters snippet? especially the memcpy and PCIe stall metrics.

nate: snippet from the nsys summary: 
```
CUDA memcpy HtoD: 230ms total, 18% of timeline
PCIe Rx stalls: 12 peaks > 10ms
CPU timeline: host_dequant_batch x 48 runs, avg=22.4ms
```

nate: trace link: https://perfetto.gp/example/trace/abcd1234 (private) — see CPU lane, search for `host_dequant_batch` markers :eyes:

perf-bot: Trace uploaded to workspace/trace-artifacts/1830456000/run_int8_kv_warmup.trace (size: 62MB)

aaron: two quick hypotheses:
1) Host dequant does memory-bound operations on the CPU and then issues synchronous cudaMemcpy which stalls the CPU/GPU pipeline
2) Our kernel selection for small batches picks an INT8 kernel that expects already-dequantized input (we then dequant on host) — could we switch to a fused kernel that includes dequant on-GPU?

lisa: on the batching side, if the adaptive window is too small we pay a lot of kernel-launch overhead. Increasing the window to 6-8ms for low-QPS routes might amortize these host dequant costs. Also consider batching by KV key to avoid repeated dequant for the same KV prefix.

michelle: follow-up experiment ideas:
- 1) Run with host dequant disabled and use fused GPU dequant kernel to compare (flag: --use-gpu-dequant)
- 2) Increase batching window from 3ms -> 8ms and measure p50/p95 latencies + tokens/sec
- 3) Try async memcpy (cudaMemcpyAsync) with a pinned staging buffer to avoid CPU stall

nate: I ran test 1 and 3 locally: switching to GPU fused-dequant reduced end-to-end p95 by 22% on small batches. Async memcpy cut CPU-blocking gaps but increased GPU memory churn and occasional hiccups when memory is tight.

sam: do we have an easy way to toggle kernel selection at runtime? If we can route small batches to fused-dequant kernels and large batches to the optimized int8-only fast path, we might get the best of both.

aaron: yes, runtime supports kernel variants. But we need perf signatures to decide the threshold. We should create a microbenchmark that sweeps batch sizes and kv-hit ratios and records: p50/p95, cpu-blocking-ms, memcpy-time, and kernel-utilization.

nate: I've started a harness in eng-runtime/perf/harnesses/int8_kv_sweep.py. Quick results:
- batch 1, kv-hit: CPU-blocking 24ms, p95 180ms
- batch 8, kv-hit: CPU-blocking 5ms, p95 98ms
- with fused-dequant: batch 1 p95 140ms

lisa: actionable next steps:
- Run full sweep on our CI cluster to capture cross-GPU variance (assign to eng-runtime perf job)
- Prototype kernel-routing rule: if expected batch_size <= 2 OR kv_hit_rate >= 0.6 -> fused-dequant kernel; else int8-fastpath
- Add metric for "host-dequant-time" to console trace breakdown so we can correlate at token level

michelle: also add a flag to Dedicated config to prefer GPU-dequant for low-latency tiers. Could help enterprise customers with strict p95.

nate: I'll write up a short doc with the perf traces + recommended kernel-routing rules and the harness results. Will post the CI sweep once it's done. Thanks for the triage so far :thumbsup:

perf-bot: CI perf job queued: eng-runtime/int8-kv-sweep #452 (ETA ~45m)

sam: great, thanks — please tag me on the doc. If CI reproduces, we should schedule a short sync to land the routing change and the console metric.

nate: will do. Leaving the trace artifact in the perf bucket and assigning follow-ups in the ticket: PERF-789.

lisa: nice work. small note: check that fused GPU dequant preserves numerical parity within our eval thresholds — we saw tiny shifts in logits in prior tests.

nate: yup will include the eval set comparison in the CI run (we run 3 eval prompts).
